title: Effect of Withdrawals on the IncomeShield Benefit Base — Fixed Indexed Annuities
content:
## Rider provision: benefit base reductions (Ashgrove Fixed Indexed Annuities, IncomeShield tiers)

**Before lifetime withdrawals start.** On an Ashgrove IncomeShield contract before lifetime withdrawals start, every withdrawal reduces the benefit base in the proportion it reduces the contract value.

**After lifetime withdrawals start.** Withdrawals within the annual lifetime withdrawal amount do not reduce the benefit base. The part of any withdrawal above the annual lifetime withdrawal amount — other than a required minimum distribution where the tier treats a required minimum distribution above that amount as not excess — reduces the benefit base proportionally.

**Size of a reduction.** A proportional reduction is the benefit base multiplied by the reducing amount, divided by the contract value from which the withdrawal is taken, rounded to the cent. The reducing amount is the whole withdrawal before lifetime withdrawals start, and the part above the annual lifetime withdrawal amount after they start.

### Input — judgement — output

| Timing | Withdrawal | Reducing amount |
|---|---|---|
| Before lifetime withdrawals start | any withdrawal | the whole withdrawal |
| After lifetime withdrawals start | within the annual lifetime withdrawal amount | none |
| After lifetime withdrawals start | above the annual lifetime withdrawal amount, not a required minimum distribution | the part above that amount |
| After lifetime withdrawals start | a required minimum distribution above the annual lifetime withdrawal amount, on a tier that treats it as not excess | none |

### Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

1. *Before lifetime withdrawals start.* Benefit base 130000; contract value 100000; withdrawal 10000. Reduction: 130000 multiplied by 10000, divided by 100000, is 13000.00; the benefit base becomes 117000.00.
2. *After lifetime withdrawals start.* Annual lifetime withdrawal amount 8000; benefit base 160000; contract value 120000; a single withdrawal of 11000. The part above 8000 is 3000. Reduction: 160000 multiplied by 3000, divided by 120000, is 4000.00.
3. *After lifetime withdrawals start, a withdrawal of 7500 against an annual lifetime withdrawal amount of 8000.* The withdrawal is within the amount; the benefit base is not reduced.
4. *After lifetime withdrawals start, a required minimum distribution of 9500 against an annual lifetime withdrawal amount of 8000, on an IncomeShield tier that treats such a distribution as not excess.* No reduction.

The benefit base is not a cash value: a reduction changes the base on which lifetime withdrawals and the rider fee are figured, and pays nothing out.
